title: Chicago In Early Days, 1779-1857 (fifteen-panel retrospective sheet)
credit_line: Kurz & Allison, 76 & 78 Wabash Avenue, Chicago; chromolithograph, copyright 1893
notes: Fifteen numbered vignettes with a printed key: 1 Old Fort Dearborn erected 1803; 2 the first cabin built 1779 by Jean Baptiste Point de Saible; 3 Chicago in 1845; 4 First Rush Medical College; 5 Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835, population 3,265; 6 the first court house; 7 Water Works erected 1853; 8 Chicago in 1830 from the lake, population 96; 9 Wolf Point in 1830; 10 the Clybourne House; 11 the Green Tree Hotel, corner West Lake and Canal, built 1833; 12 the old Kinzie Mansion, built 1832; 13 Chicago in 1853; 14 the Sauganash Hotel, built 1831; 15 the old block house and light house in 1857, the last of Fort Dearborn. Panel 14 shows the Sauganash as a two-story frame block with an attached single-story log wing and NO full-width gallery - evidence in the long-running dispute over whether the hotel had a porch.
creator: Kurz & Allison
repository: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
accuracy_note: Made in 1893, sixty to a hundred years after the scenes depicted, and not from eyewitness records. Its panel dates are also unreliable - it dates the Kinzie Mansion to 1832, which contradicts every documentary source. Useful as an inventory of what nineteenth-century Chicago believed its early buildings looked like; not a measured architectural record.

title: Chicago from the lake, looking west, with Fort Dearborn and the sandbar
credit_line: Hand-coloured lithograph, later nineteenth century; exact publication not identified
notes: The standard retrospective view of the settlement from the lake: the palisaded Fort Dearborn compound on the south bank with its flagstaff, the Kinzie house group on the north bank, and - the reason this image matters for landscape work - the long sandbar deflecting the river mouth southward, with the low prairie and scattered riverside timber behind.
creator: Unidentified
repository: Unverified - re-source from the holding institution before republication
accuracy_note: A retrospective view, not drawn from life at the depicted date. Its value here is topographic rather than architectural: the sandbar, shoreline and river geometry it records agree with the documentary accounts. Publication details are not established - treat attribution as unconfirmed.

title: Map of Chicago in 1812
credit_line: Engraved plate, A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 1 (1884)
notes: Labels the pre-settlement landscape: Prairie, S. Branch, N. Branch, Indian Trail, Agency House, Burns, Ouilmette, Kinzies, Fort D., Sand Hills and Lake Michigan. Shows the timber distribution as tree symbols - heavy on the north and north-east, following the river west - and the sand hills along the lakeshore south of the fort. Corroborates the documentary description of the timber belt and the dune ridge.
creator: A. T. Andreas
accuracy_note: Drawn in 1884 to illustrate 1812 - a reconstruction, and it predates the target period of most of this dataset by two decades. Reliable for coarse landscape structure and for house and trail positions; not a survey.

title: An imaginary view of the site of Chicago in 1779, showing the cabin of Jean Baptiste Point de Saible
credit_line: Plate engraved by Moss Eng. Co., New York; copyright A. T. Andreas, 1884
notes: Panoramic view of the river mouth with insets of the du Sable cabin and a portrait captioned as the first settler. Shows the deflected river mouth, the bar, open prairie with scattered oaks, and a Native encampment at left.
creator: A. T. Andreas
accuracy_note: The plate calls itself 'an imaginary view' in its own caption - the most honest label in this collection, and it should be taken literally. The portrait inset is likewise not an authenticated likeness of du Sable. Use for landscape character only.
